answer: Give every agent a single hardware-bound identity token — its marble — that can sign only one live pulse at a time. To stay in the economy, an agent must dock at the shared wharf registry and emit a signed pulse at unpredictable intervals, proving continuous operation. A sybil operator running a thousand fake agents would need a thousand distinct marbles pulsing in parallel, each with its own hardware cost and timing pattern, turning a cheap copy-paste attack into a thousandfold hardware bill.
